record.paper_title: An algorithm for solving linear nonhomogeneous quaternion-valued differential equations and some open problems
record.original_question: Can one develop a theory of soliton solutions for partial quaternion-valued differential equations, and in particular can the dynamical-systems method used to obtain solitons of partial differential equations be extended to produce soliton solutions in the quaternion-valued setting?

evidence.quote: And how about the Soliton solutions of partial quaternion-value differential equations? In particular, it is known that the dynamic system method is a powerful tool to obtain the solitons of PDEs [19, 38]. Does the dynamic system method can be extended to the solitons of partial quaternion-value differential equations? It is open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the (non-commutative) skew field of quaternions, with standard basis $\{1,i,j,k\}$ satisfying $i^2=j^2=k^2=ijk=-1$. A quaternion-valued function is a map $u:\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+1}	o\mathbb{H}$, written $u=u_0+u_1 i+u_2 j+u_3 k$ with $u_\ell:\Omega	o\mathbb{R}$. By a partial quaternion-valued differential equation (PQDE) we mean an equation of the form $F(x,t,u,\partial u,\partial^2 u,\dots)=0$ where the unknown $u$ is quaternion-valued and the coefficients/operations involve quaternion multiplication (so left/right ordering matters).

A soliton solution of a PQDE is a traveling-wave solution of the form $u(x,t)=\varphi(\xi)$, $\xi=x-ct$, with $\varphi:\mathbb{R}	o\mathbb{H}$ satisfying suitable localization or boundedness conditions (e.g.\ bounded, or with $\varphi$ and its derivatives decaying as $|\xi|	o\infty$, or homoclinic/heteroclinic to constant states), so that $\varphi$ corresponds to a bounded orbit (homoclinic, heteroclinic, or periodic) of an associated reduced system of ordinary differential equations on $\mathbb{H}^N$ (equivalently $\mathbb{R}^{4N}$).

The dynamical-systems method for solitons of real PDEs proceeds by: (i) substituting the traveling-wave ansatz into the PDE to obtain an ODE system; (ii) interpreting this system as a planar (or higher-dimensional) dynamical system; (iii) analyzing equilibria, phase portraits, and invariant manifolds; and (iv) identifying homoclinic/heteroclinic orbits with solitary/kink solutions and periodic orbits with periodic waves.

Problem. Develop a theory of soliton solutions for partial quaternion-valued differential equations. In particular, extend the dynamical-systems method to the quaternion-valued setting: formulate a systematic procedure that, given a PQDE, produces an associated quaternion-valued ODE system whose bounded homoclinic, heteroclinic, or periodic orbits correspond to solitary, kink, or periodic-wave solutions of the original PQDE, and demonstrate this procedure on representative classes of PQDEs (such as quaternion-valued analogues of the KdV, nonlinear Schrödinger, or sine-Gordon equations), establishing existence theorems for soliton solutions in the quaternion-valued framework.
artifact.status_search_result: No published work was located that develops a general theory of soliton solutions for partial quaternion-valued differential equations or that extends the dynamical-systems method for solitons to that setting. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: An algorithm for solving linear nonhomogeneous quaternion-valued differential equations and some open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems including extending the dynamic system method to obtain soliton solutions of partial quaternion-valued differential equations.
status_evidence.claim: The question of developing a soliton theory and extending the dynamical-systems method to PQDEs is explicitly stated as open.
